top_module.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
top_module.description: Top-level digital controller integrating MMIO, request framing, response deframing, freshness/timeout supervision, actuator mapping, clamp logic, and fallback selection for an external aerodynamics runtime.
top_module.functionality: Implements the full external-runtime control contract. The module accepts compact host configuration through a small memory-mapped register window, creates bounded request frames containing only metadata, tracks one outstanding request by default, validates and correlates inbound response frames, checks freshness and timeout thresholds, enforces velocity-envelope and response-status rules, maps accepted response recommendations into actuator commands, clamps commands to configured limits, and selects a deterministic safe fallback pattern on timeout, stale, malformed, or operating-condition violation conditions. The design is synthesizable and FPGA-oriented, using only small state, counters, comparators, and bounded FIFOs/BRAM-backed storage.
responsibilities: Expose the MMIO register window and produce deterministic readback.
Generate bounded request frames with sequence number, geometry handle, flow-condition metadata, velocity, and flags.
Hold a single outstanding request unless configured otherwise within implemented bounds.
Accept only valid response frames with matching sequence and acceptable status.
Reject out-of-envelope velocity requests and malformed or stale responses.
Produce actuator commands only after validation and clamp each setpoint to configured bounds.
Assert fault_o whenever fallback is active or a rejection/timeout/operating-condition violation is detected.
Keep all outputs deterministic during reset and fault conditions.
top_module.reset_behavior: On rst_n deassertion, all configuration and status registers clear to deterministic defaults, outstanding-request state is cleared, FIFOs are emptied or invalidated, request/response tracking sequence state is initialized from the seed register default, act_valid and req_valid deassert, req_data and act_data become deterministic safe values, fault_o deasserts unless a default violation is encoded by configuration, and fallback control is placed into its safe actuator pattern.
behavior_rules: All logic shall be fully synchronous to clk with active-low reset rst_n.
cfg_ready shall assert for implemented register accesses and may deassert or ignore writes to unmapped locations without causing X-propagation.
cfg_rdata shall return valid readback for implemented registers and a defined value for unmapped addresses.
Request frames shall contain only compact metadata and no raw geometry arrays, flow fields, or model tensors.
The outbound request channel shall not change req_data while req_valid is asserted and req_ready is low.
At most one request may be outstanding unless the configuration explicitly enables a bounded expansion that remains finite and synthesizable.
The controller shall reject velocities outside the configured 20 to 55 m/s operating envelope.
Responses with mismatched sequence, invalid status, or expired freshness/timeout shall be discarded and mapped to fallback.
Actuator commands shall be clamped to configured min/max bounds before act_valid is asserted.
Safe fallback shall be deterministic and selected on timeout, stale response, malformed response, operating-condition violation, or external-service-unavailable indication.
fault_o shall assert whenever fallback is active or a reject/violation condition exists.

modules.name: aero_mmio_register_window
modules.description: Compact memory-mapped register interface that stores configuration, status, sequence seed, threshold controls, and last-accepted readback values. This module decodes cfg_valid/cfg_write/cfg_addr/cfg_wdata and exposes explicit semantic control and status signals to the control core.
modules.functionality: Implements the implemented register map for configuration and status access. It captures timeout threshold, freshness threshold, actuator min/max bounds, velocity envelope min/max, enable bits, and sequence seed, while also providing readback of status, last accepted sequence number, and last issued actuator command. Writes outside the implemented map are ignored or return a defined status indication through cfg_ready/cfg_rdata behavior.
responsibilities: Decode host register accesses.
Store configuration fields and expose them as semantic outputs.
Provide deterministic readback of status and last values.
Ignore or safely flag writes to unmapped addresses.
Never infer large data structures or store bulk payloads as registers.
modules.reset_behavior: Registers reset to deterministic defaults: enable bits deasserted or set to the documented safe configuration, thresholds initialized to conservative values, sequence seed initialized to a fixed default, cfg_ready deasserted when idle, cfg_rdata returns defined reset values, and no transient write side effects are emitted on reset release.
behavior_rules: Implemented register addresses shall correspond to configuration, status, seed, and readback fields only.
Unimplemented addresses shall not corrupt state.
Status inputs shall be sampled synchronously and made available for readback.
No bulk payload storage shall be implemented in registers.
All semantic configuration outputs shall be stable between writes.

modules.name: aero_request_framer
modules.description: Creates bounded outbound request frames containing only metadata needed by the external aerodynamics runtime. It packages request type, sequence number, geometry handle, flow-condition metadata, velocity, and flags, while ensuring the request data remains stable until handshake completion.
modules.functionality: Generates a compact framed request for an asynchronous external DoMINO runtime. The request carries only compact metadata and a geometry identifier or payload handle; the module does not deserialize STL or large geometry internally. The framer enforces a bounded outstanding-request policy of at most one by default, holds req_data stable while waiting for handshake completion, and flags busy and velocity violation states to downstream supervision.
responsibilities: Assemble outbound request metadata into a fixed-width frame.
Maintain req_valid and req_data stability until req_ready handshake completion.
Expose a bounded request_outstanding indication.
Flag operating-envelope violations on velocity metadata.
Avoid any unbounded queueing or heavy compute.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, request framing is idle, req_valid is low, req_data is deterministic, outstanding state is cleared, sequence state is initialized from cfg_sequence_seed default, and busy/velocity_violation are deasserted unless configuration explicitly encodes a default violation.
behavior_rules: The request frame shall contain only metadata and no model tensors or raw geometry arrays.
Sequence numbering shall be deterministic and correlated with accepted requests.
If request generation is disabled, req_valid shall remain low.
The module shall never allow more than one outstanding request unless an explicit bounded configuration is added.

modules.name: aero_response_deframer
modules.description: Validates and parses the inbound response stream from the external runtime, checking packet status, sequence correlation, and freshness before exposing semantic control recommendations. Invalid, stale, mismatched, or timeout-related responses are discarded and translated into fallback indicators.
modules.functionality: Consumes 128-bit response frames, validates sequence correlation and status code, applies freshness and timeout policy, and exposes parsed response semantics only when the frame is acceptable. It provides explicit reject outputs for stale, timeout, and malformed conditions, and produces a response_accepted pulse only when the response is valid and fresh.
responsibilities: Parse the compact response frame.
Correlate response sequence against the outstanding request.
Validate status code and freshness.
Suppress malformed or mismatched responses.
Provide deterministic reject signaling for supervision.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, rsp_ready is deasserted until the controller is able to accept responses, response outputs are cleared to deterministic values, and all reject/accept indications are low.
behavior_rules: Responses with mismatched sequence numbers shall be rejected.
Responses with invalid status codes shall be rejected as malformed.
Responses exceeding freshness or timeout policy shall be rejected.
The module shall not infer any heavy compute or model behavior.

modules.name: aero_actuator_mapper
modules.description: Maps validated response recommendations into a bounded actuator command, clamps the command to configured min/max limits, and provides fallback selection when required. The command is emitted only after validation and is deterministic in fault states.
modules.functionality: Transforms response recommendations into a bounded actuator output command. It clamps each setpoint to the configured min/max limits before asserting act_valid, and it selects a deterministic safe fallback actuator pattern whenever the response path is rejected, timed out, stale, malformed, or operating conditions are violated. The module reports whether clamping occurred and whether fallback is currently active.
responsibilities: Convert parsed response hints into actuator command words.
Clamp command values to configured bounds before emission.
Emit a safe fallback pattern when required.
Hold deterministic outputs during fault conditions and reset.
Provide readback of the last issued actuator command.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, act_valid is low, act_data is set to a deterministic safe fallback pattern, clamp_active and fallback_active are deasserted or set to the defined reset-safe condition, and last_actuator_command is cleared to the safe default.
behavior_rules: All actuator setpoints shall be clamped within configured min/max limits before output.
Fallback shall override any non-accepted response condition.
The module shall not depend on external runtime availability for safe behavior.
Outputs shall remain deterministic in fault conditions.
